data.narrative:
ISEE, a Series B-stage autonomous systems company founded by Yibiao Zhao, operates within the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation landscape comprises eight private peers—including Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation—with no direct public comparables available for benchmarking.

Valuation triangulation relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to ISEE's $70M total capital raised, implying a post-money valuation of $133M. This multiplier reflects typical progression mechanics from Series B to subsequent rounds within the sector. A traditional Peer-Median approach proved inapplicable: while five same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap emerged within narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies). Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of the Drones & Autonomous space.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $113M (low) to $153M (high), centered on $133M. This estimate carries meaningful uncertainty inherent to single-method derivation and the absence of near-peer financial data at comparable stages. Key sensitivities include ISEE's specific operational metrics relative to the broader peer set and market conditions affecting subsequent-round pricing in autonomous systems. Validation would benefit from expanded peer financial disclosure or management guidance on unit economics and deployment trajectory.
